claim: Adding ExcludeFromCodeCoverage to the generated partial declaration of a user-declared resolver breaks resolvers that already have that attribute. ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute does not allow multiples, so the attributes from the user's and generated partial declarations merge and produce CS0579, turning a reasonable pre-upgrade workaround into a compile error.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.GeneratedExcludeFromCodeCoverageTests.ExistingExcludeFromCodeCoverageOnResolverDoesNotDuplicateAttribute. Its source declares a [GeneratedMessagePackResolver] partial resolver that is already decorated with [ExcludeFromCodeCoverage]; compilation succeeds on base and should fail on head with an unexpected CS0579 duplicate-attribute diagnostic.

claim: The per-type coverage assertion is only per-file: it passes when a generated file contains one attribute, so removing ExcludeFromCodeCoverage from FormatterCache<T> or the resolver's GetFormatterHelper is not detected even though the test claims every generated type is decorated.

claim: The target-framework test checks preprocessor text but never compiles the generated output with target-framework symbols. RunGeneratorsAndUpdateCompilation discards both the output compilation and diagnostics, so malformed generated syntax or an unavailable attribute can satisfy the acceptance-critical compilation requirement unnoticed.
